The VENT+ pathway addresses an important gap in care for patients recovering from critical illness. Patients typically have complex medical needs, moderate to high frailty, and functional, cognitive, or social changes following an ICU stay, often requiring caregiver support and coordination across multiple providers and care settings. VENT+ uses an interdisciplinary, whole-person approach, bringing together occupational therapy, physiotherapy, social work, psychiatry, respiratory care, and other clinical expertise. The team supports patients and caregivers while giving providers a collaborative forum to problem-solve, share expertise and navigate care needs. The program aims to improve patient and caregiver experience, recovery and quality of life, care coordination, avoidable acute-care utilization, and provider experience and satisfaction. Position Summary The Nurse Practitioner, Clinical Care Facilitator is a core member of the VENT+ interdisciplinary team, providing advanced clinical care and case management for patients transitioning from ICU to the community. Working closely with the interdisciplinary team, including OT, PT and Social Work, the Nurse Practitioner leads comprehensive assessments, develops individualized care and recovery plans, and coordinates care across hospital, primary care, specialist and community settings. Over the approximately 18-month pathway, the Nurse Practitioner works in partnership with patients and caregivers to monitor progress, address evolving needs, and support patients in achieving their individual recovery goals. The role also works closely with primary care providers and other members of the care team to support safe transitions, strengthen continuity of care, and optimize recovery and quality of life.
